cells.title: E2b · 达·芬奇(主) + 卡拉瓦乔(辅)
cells.lead: Fusion of two painterly languages: Leonardo da Vinci dominant (70%), Caravaggio secondary (30%).
cells.main_segment: Renaissance oil painting in the manner of Leonardo da Vinci, sfumato: absolutely no hard contours anywhere, every light-to-shadow transition is a wide, continuous grey gradient, soft smoky modelling; single soft light from the upper left moulding forms out of deep shadow; aerial perspective — distant forms turn blue-grey, lose saturation and dissolve into haze; narrow earth palette of ochre, umber, muted blue and dull gold, overall low saturation; rocks shaped like rounded cones, wet atmosphere over shallow green water; invisible brushwork, glazed surface, matte, aged varnish warmth; contemplative, quiet, mysterious mood
cells.aux_segment: Caravaggio-style tenebrist oil painting: one single hard directional light from high left, no fill light, no reflected light; background areas in near-black shadow (values under 10% of the lit highlights); deep dark brown ground left visible inside the shadows as their mid-tone; violent chiaroscuro: lit passages bright and warm, shadows crushed, midtones suppressed; one frozen instant of dramatic action; the main motif pushed flat against the picture plane and cropped by the frame edge; restrained earth palette — ochre, madder red, lead white, bitumen black, one or two saturated accents; direct painting, broad final touches, impasto highlights on the lit edges

cells.title: E2c · 莫奈(主) + 塞尚(辅)

main.source: §8.1 正向段（4 卡注记口径）

cells.lead: Fusion of two painterly languages: Claude Monet dominant (70%), Paul Cézanne secondary (30%).
cells.partition: Split the scene into two explicit layers at the horizon: the sky and the distant water layer follow the atmospheric envelope — soft haze, a gradual falling-off of contrast confined to this layer, colour gathered into one air tone; the mid-ground and foreground layer (rocks, waves, the lighthouse) follows the structural treatment — compressed space, near and far forms at the same scale, shifting viewpoints, and no fog or haze colour in this near layer.
cells.main_segment: oil painting in the style of Claude Monet, french impressionism, en plein air, broken comma-like brushwork with unblended strokes laid side by side, light-toned ground and high-key palette, coloured shadows (blue-violet) instead of black, atmospheric envelope unifying the whole scene, soft haze and shimmering water with broken reflections, asymmetrical cropped composition with no linear perspective and no three-dimensional modelling, water surface occupying a large portion of the canvas, sky and water mirroring each other, palette: pale blue, lavender, rose, cream, turquoise, soft green, pale yellow; soft edges dissolving between colour patches
cells.aux_segment: Late Cézanne landscape in the manner of his late period (1895–1906): the entire surface built from short, visible parallel brushstrokes (taches) of 0.5–1.5 cm equivalent, arranged in groups of 4–8 directional families that both model volume and unify the picture plane; forms constructed only by color modulation — light, half-tone and quarter-tone steps of ochre, orange, olive, viridian, cobalt and ultramarine — never by black shading; forms carry broken, multiple outlines, 30% of contour segments left open so forms merge into the background; a network of blue in shadows, contours and sky (12–15% of pixels); sky and earth painted with equal substance, no atmospheric recession, distant forms the same scale as near ones; shifting viewpoints within one frame; 5–8% of the canvas left thinly covered or bare, suggesting unfinish; dry, matte oil surface, fine canvas weave visible.
cells.main_negative: hard black outlines, chiaroscuro, dark varnished browns, smooth blending, photographic detail, crisp vector edges, studio lighting, neon saturation, 3D modelling, symmetrical centred composition, depth of field, HDR
cells.aux_negative: --no chiaroscuro, black cast shadows, single-point perspective, atmospheric haze, photorealistic detail, smooth blended gradients, glossy varnish, palette-knife impasto (that is the 1860s style), narrative action, dramatic poses, facial expression detail, high-contrast lighting, neon colors
